title: Middle school algebra: simplify and model
description: Four lessons from like terms to word-problem models: combine, distribute, simplify-then-evaluate, and translate situations into expressions.
assumptions: Variables stand for whole numbers in examples; expressions are linear. No network or apparatus needed.
stage1goal: Build combining and distributing from evidence.
stage2goal: Simplify strategically and model new situations.
like-terms.title: Like terms combine
like-terms.goal: Identify like terms and combine their coefficients.
like-terms.reading: Only terms with the same variable part combine: 3x + 2x = 5x, but 3x + 2y stays.
like-terms.worked.fb: Same variable part means same kind of quantity.
like-terms.match.prompt: Match each sum to its simplified form.
like-terms.match.hint: Add the numbers in front of same letters.
like-terms.match.l1.label: 3x + 2x
like-terms.match.l2.label: 5y - y
like-terms.match.l3.label: 4a + a
like-terms.match.r1.label: 5x
like-terms.match.r2.label: 4y
like-terms.match.r3.label: 5a
like-terms.c1.a.label: 4x and 9x
like-terms.c1.b.label: 4x and 4y
distribute.title: Distribute then combine
distribute.goal: Use the distributive law to expand and then combine.
distribute.reading: a(b + c) = ab + ac. Expand first, then combine like terms.
distribute.worked.prompt: In your own words: what does 3(x + 4) become?
distribute.transfer-area.prompt: A rectangle is 3 wide and (x + 4) long. Its area splits into 3x and 12. With x = 5, total area?
distribute.c1.a.label: 2x + 5
distribute.c1.b.label: 2x + 10
simplify-first.title: Simplify before substituting
simplify-first.goal: Choose the efficient order: simplify, then evaluate.
simplify-first.reading: Simplifying first reduces arithmetic: 2x + 3x + 4 at x = 6 is 5x + 4 = 34, not three separate products.
simplify-first.struggle: Without computing, explain why simplifying 2x + 3x + 4 before substituting x = 6 is easier than substituting first.
simplify-first.worked.prompt: What is the efficient order and why?
simplify-first.worked.fb: Combine like terms first, then substitute once.
simplify-first.worked.content: 2x + 3x + 4 = 5x + 4; at x = 6 gives 34 with one multiplication.
simplify-first.order.prompt: Order the steps: substitute, combine like terms, distribute.
simplify-first.order.d.label: Distribute
simplify-first.order.c.label: Combine like terms
simplify-first.order.s.label: Substitute
simplify-first.independent.prompt: Simplify 4x + x + 7 then evaluate at x = 3.
simplify-first.c1.prompt: Best first step for 3x + 2x + 5 at x = 4?
simplify-first.c1.a.label: Combine 3x + 2x
simplify-first.c1.b.label: Substitute x = 4 everywhere
model-situations.title: Model situations with expressions
model-situations.goal: Translate a situation into an expression and evaluate it.
model-situations.reading: A model names the quantity per unit and the count: cost = price per ticket times tickets plus fixed fee.
model-situations.worked.prompt: What two parts does a cost model need?
model-situations.worked.fb: A per-unit rate times count, plus any fixed amount.
model-situations.worked.content: Tickets: 8 each plus 5 booking fee gives 8n + 5.
model-situations.perimeter.prompt: A rectangle is x long and 3 wide. Which expression is its perimeter?
model-situations.perimeter.a.label: 2x + 6
model-situations.perimeter.b.label: 3x
model-situations.transfer-tickets.prompt: Tickets cost 8 each plus a 5 fee. Total for 6 tickets?
model-situations.c1.prompt: n books at 7 each plus 2 shipping:
model-situations.c1.a.label: 7 + 2n
model-situations.c1.b.label: 7n + 2
model-situations.c1.b.fb: Per-book rate times count plus fixed.
